There are a few things to be aware of with this game.

1. This is not in Early Access or Beta anymore. As of April 22nd, 2019 this game is officially version 1.0. Things are pretty quiet from the developer so it is likely that any and all changes/tweaks to the game will be from the community via mods.

2. This game is not built on a pre-existing game engine and is not super optimized. It is a labor of love with some rough edges. I can run it on maximum 1080p settings on my Lenovo Yoga laptop, but it sounds like I am flying an airplane at takeoff.

3. The graphics are not the reason to play this game. The depth of the game mechanics are the main draw. And yes, it is a niche game for tech nerds. You want to build a custom PC and go for the top of the overclocking leaderboard? Sure! Want to set up several powerful machines to mine for BitCoin? Go for it! Want to find ways to swindle customers by swapping their expensive hardware for a cheaper part? Uh... yeah, you can do that. Want to build your own line of PCs and sell them in your shop? Yep!

4. Try the demo before you buy. If you find the tutorial boring, keep in mind that you can select Expert difficulty in the main game which makes things much more challenging. But, if you find the demo hard and tedious, this probably isn't the game for you. And that is ok.

5. There are a lot of things that aren't fully explained. Updating the OS, filtering shop parts via the dots at the end of the tabs, the error code beeps... some things you have to Google. And unfortunately Google doesn't have all the answers.

All that being said, if you like this game you can easily spend hours playing. Like it enough and you may decide to try your hand at modding. If you need help, the best place to look is in the community guides section here on Steam.

ซึ่งเริ่มเกมมาคุณจะมีร้านคอมเล็กๆร้านนี่ ที่มีชั้นวางของ โต๊ะแคชเชียร์เท่านั้น ถ้าเป็นเกมอื่นนั้นมีร้านมาแบบนี้เรากดซื้่อของแล้วของจะมาบนชั้นวางของทันที แต่เกมนี้คุณต้องรอครับ หลังจากคุณสั่งสินค้าเสร็จแล้ว คุณต้องรอพนักงานมาส่งของให้ ซึ่งเกมจะแนะนำให้กดเร่งเวลาให้เร็วขึ้นจนกว่าพนักงานจะมา และถ้าของมาถึงแล้ว ของจะไม่ขึ้นชั้นวางของด้วยตัวเองนะครับ คุณต้องเซ็นรับ แกะกล่องแล้วนำไปชั้นวางของของร้านก่อนจะนำไปยังชั้นวางของที่ใช้ขายของ 

ตรงนี้คุณอาจขายคาดหวังว่าเกมมันจะแค่ขายของก็รวยได้แล้ว แต่มันไม่ง่ายเช่นนั้น ถึงแม้ลุกค้าเต็มถนน แต่คุณต้องรอให้ลุกค้าเข้ามาในร้าน ซึ่งในระหว่างนั้นคุณต้องกดเร่งเวลา เพื่อรอลูกค้าเข้่าร้าน แต่ด้วยเหตุผลกลใดไม่ทราบ ลูกค้าทื่สามารถอยู่ในร้านในเวลาเดียวก้นจะถูกจำกัดด้วยขนาดของร้าน โดยร้านเริ่มต้นนั้นจะจำกัดแค่ 1 คน คุณยังสามารถขยายร้านได้เพื่อรองรับลูกค้าเพิ่ม แต่ไม่ว่ายังคุณก็ไม่มีวันที่จะเห็นลูกค้าเป็น 10 อยุ่ในร้านเวลาเดียวกันอยู่ดี นอกจากนี้ลูกค้าที่เข้ามาจะมีส่วนน้อยที่สนใจสินค้าบนชั้นวางของส่วนใหญ่จะสั่งของชิ้นนั้นผ่านผู้เล่นแล้วคุณต้องสั่งของให้พนักงานส่งของมาส่งอีกที 

จากที่บอกไปข้างต้นการขายของบนชั้นวางของนั้นไม่ได้ทำเงินอะไรมากมายนัก แต่สิ่งที่ทำเงินนั้นคือทำตามคำสั่งลูกค้าครับ นอกจากรับออเดอร์สั่งของอย่างเดียวแล้วคุณยังต้องแก้ปัญหาให้ลูกค้าต่างๆนาๆ เช่นซ่อมคอมที่เสีย อัพเกรดคอมให้ลูกค้าพร้อม driver จัดคอมตามสเปค ทำลายไวรัสในคอม ลง Windoor(คุณอ่านไม่ผิดชือนี้จริงๆ) ให้ลูกค้า แต่นอกจากจัดคอมสเปคที่ลูกค้าต้องการเงินทำอย่างอื่นนั้นไม่ได้มากมายอะไรนัก ซึ่งตรงนี้คือจุดที่ยากที่สุดของเกมคือการหาเงิน

I get it, it has the potential to be a fun game, if you manage to figure your way through the tutorial. Basically it says: "Do this" and you are given no choice but to try to figure out what to click. Some things are natural for experienced system builders like applying thermal paste to the CPU (clearly shown with arrows btw), but other things are not so obvious.

Downloading drivers for the hardware ingame is more difficult than IRL, you have to remember what exact model number of say the graphics card you've installed, there is no generic "Download latest NVidia driver" or a DVD/USB stick that comes with the card with the drivers that you could have used.

It's fun to build custom PCs and fill em up with 8 x 2TB SSDs, but it is not so fun trying to figure out the menu/icons before you go bankrupt. The tutorial needs some serious rework. As of now, the game is only usable in Sandbox mode, simulating a system build, but not as a game - unless you plan to spend 4 hours trying to figure out the GUI. So [b]for now[/b], thumbs down - if they rework the tutorial and streamline a bit more i may change my opinion.

Unfortunately it's a no from me, and I really gave this game a lot of time to develop, before submitting this review. It's just too boring and lacking in information. 

So you start out and the first thing you discover is downloading drivers is a big pain in the rear. So you build and set up a file server to make things smoother. So now you've got like 100 different drivers for all types of motherboards and video cards. If I'm downloading a video driver irl I just select my OS and Card and it pretty much gets the same driver no matter what card I choose. This game has  like 12 or more video card drivers. Motherboard drivers are nearly infinite.  Each motherboard is divided by brand, then type, then model number. Expect to be looking at your PC 3 or 5 times to verify the motherboard model number. It's not easy.

Then there's the waiting. When you start the game you'll wait anywhere between 24 to 36 hours before your first customer comes in. There's no way to get business faster, it just is what it is. From there on you'll be getting new customers at the same rate for as long as I've played. They all have fairly easy to diagnose problems and you can cheat them out of hardware very easily. Meanwhile your storefront will suffer from lack of inventory, but if you buy stuff to place out there no one will buy it. So your best model of income is to do the bare minimum to repair your customers PC's and steal what you can in parts from them, while not stocking your store with anything of value. 

This has been the main way to play the game for the last year I've owned it. Why would this appeal to anyone? I guess trolls would like it, but beyond that, this game really suffers.

En exemple, le fait de devoir installer des pilotes ainsi que des win différents, pouvoir vendre des articles ou des pc fait soi-même , avoir des "mini-jeux" lors de la mise en place des ventilateurs ou alimentation, les missions qui sont plus riches et toujours différentes, car les clients ont des restrictions plus développées et j'en passe..

Before I get started, here's a tiny bit of background on myself: 
I've been playing games since 1987. I was 4 years old. I've played everything and every genre out there. Over the last 10-15 years just about everything feels the same with of course just a few exceptions, and this has made me super-critical over time. Maybe I'm just getting old and cranky. But, with my being critical, if I actually like something, I feel like people should make note of that. 

Review:
Hardware Engineers to me feels fresh and new. The creativity that has gone into this game has been amazing. Even the cheeky humor with major brand name changes like MZI and Entil add charm to the game. I love it. I burned a lot of hours playing this game on just one playthrough. The detail in fixing computers is such that it has complexity and depth without being too difficult, and simple enough that just about anyone can play it without being boring. 

Other games that gave me the same feeling of being fresh and new while setting themselves apart from all the others and have left lasting memories are Stardew Valley, Rimworld, and Subnautica. With that said, I feel Hardware Engineers deserves to be on what I would consider a list of rare gems. 

I tried grinding my way through PC Building Simulator hoping it would stop boring me. It didn't. While Hardware Engineers doesn't compete with it graphically, I feel it has more promise, more charm, better gameplay, and is overall significantly more fun. Of course PCBS is a simulator, so perhaps maybe not a fair comparison...? 

TL;DR
Hardware Engineers is among the best games I've ever played. 
Keep up the good work, and make this amazing game even more amazing!
